entry_state: A replacement premium transfers measurement without inventing cash. Future-service changes and finance use distinct rate bases. Variable-benefit allocation may require a revised rate, while changed holdings preserve the old OCI history under its own schedule.
exit_state: Loss releases preserve finance and service origins. A holdings change leaves an old OCI schedule frozen at the change-date assumptions, independent of new valuation outcomes. Derecognition now asks which original policy produced the accumulated balance.
findings: The loss component reaches zero under the supported one-fifth allocation; treating all releases as revenue plus a separate reversal would overstate profit by 21.
The old OCI reclassification is 980/121 even when actual first-year liability is changed from 130 to 132. New finance and old-balance runoff remain separate.
The reverse holdings change likewise preserves old expenses 10 and 11 while a new allocation starts independently. No new defect observed.
